LanguageData.HypovolemicShock.label: hypovolemic shock
LanguageData.HypovolemicShock.description: A life-threatening state caused by insufficient blood flow to the body. Hypovolemic shock is a medical emergency; if left untreated, the insufficient blood flow can cause damage to organs, leading to hypoxia and multiple organ failure.\n\nShock develops when blood loss exceeds 45%. Severity changes gradually with the remaining blood-volume deficit. Stopping the bleeding prevents further loss; restoring blood volume with transfusions or IV fluids allows recovery. Tending and adrenaline provide temporary support but do not replace missing blood. Existing hypoxic injuries and other complications still require treatment.
